analysis:
Free power to agriculture was a Congress election promise in Andhra Pradesh in 2004. On the day he was sworn in as Chief Minister, Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy signed an order providing free electricity to agricultural pumpsets.

The initial subsidy bill was reported at about Rs 400 crore and the scheme supplied about seven hours of power a day to farms. A Government of India (MANAGE) document records that the free power scheme was introduced in 2004 and has continued in operation since then, with the annual agriculture electricity subsidy estimated at about Rs 8,400 crore per annum in later years.

The promise was implemented immediately on assuming office; the policy question that followed concerned the fiscal cost of the subsidy, which grew substantially over time.
notes: Primary 2004 news articles (India Today, 7 June 2004; rediff.com) are referenced through the Wikipedia page but their direct URLs were not opened during research; the scheme's existence and 2004 start are corroborated by the MANAGE government document and later official statements. Quote is the reported wording, not verbatim.
